Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

betaNB 1.0.7.9001

  • Add SCorSqNB() for the image of a signed-semipartial interval under squaring.

betaNB 1.0.7.9000

Minor

  • DeltaRSqNB() gains adj = TRUE for differences in adjusted R-squared. confint() and summary() gain type = "mpc" for modified percentile intervals of Delta R-squared (sr2), unadjusted or adjusted. The sample F test uses the interval’s alpha and the unadjusted increment. Upper limits and ordinary percentile interpolation are unchanged. Existing defaults and "pc", "bc", "bca" intervals are unchanged.

  • NB() gains the wild bootstrap: type = "wild" (default "pairs", unchanged), with weights ("rademacher", "mammen", "webb", "normal"), hc ("hc3", "hc0", "hc1", "hc2", "hc4", "hc4m", "hc5"; the same leverage adjustments as betaSandwich), and x ("random" resamples the regressors with their residuals, "fixed" keeps them). The effect size functions and intervals work on the wild draws unchanged. The sampler is in R for now.

  • New FSqNB(): Cohen’s f-squared and the local f-squared of each regressor.

  • Faster bootstrap: the bootstrap and jackknife covariance matrices (closed-form leave-one-out) and the effect sizes are computed in C++ (Rcpp, RcppArmadillo), once per NB() call. The bootstrap samples are the same as before for the same seed.

  • The thetahatstar and jackknife elements of nb and betanb objects are now matrices (one draw per row) instead of lists. nb objects also hold es and es_jackknife.

  • Selective standardization: the arguments std_y and std_x standardize only y or only the named regressors (for example, leave a dummy variable in its 0-1 units). The defaults give the same results as before.
